title: 「What + 名詞（+ 主語 + 動詞）」感嘆句
titleZh: 「What + 名詞（+ 主語 + 動詞）」感嘆句
titleEn: Using What + noun in exclamative sentences

source.file: Sentence Structure 135 -「What + 名詞（+ 主語 + 動詞）」感嘆句.pdf

formula: What + a/an + (adverb) + adjective + singular countable noun + subject + verb!

formulas.formula: What + a/an + (adverb) + adjective + singular countable noun + subject + verb!
What + (adverb) + adjective + plural noun + subject + verb!
What + (adverb) + adjective + uncountable noun + subject + verb!

rules.zh: 單數可數名詞需要 a 或 an 選擇 a 或 an 時，要按照後面第一個字的讀音，而不是只看名詞： useful 以 /j/ 音開始，所以使用 a。 unusual 以元音開始，所以使用 an。
rules.en: A singular countable noun requires a or an. Choose between them according to the initial sound of the following word, not the noun alone: useful begins with a /j/ sound and takes a, while unusual begins with a vowel sound and takes an.
examples: What a beautiful house this is!
What an exciting game this is!
What a useful app this is!
What an unusual idea that is!

rules.zh: 複數及不可數名詞前不使用 a 或 an 正確： 錯誤：
rules.en: Do not use a or an before plural or uncountable nouns.
examples: What beautiful flowers these are!
What useful information she gave us!
What a beautiful flowers these are!
What an useful information she gave us!

rules.zh: 完整句使用正常陳述句字序 名詞後面使用： 正確： 錯誤： 這是感嘆句，不是疑問句，因此不使用疑問句倒裝。
rules.en: A full what-exclamation uses normal statement word order, subject + verb, after the noun phrase. It is an exclamation, not a question, so do not use interrogative inversion.
examples: What a beautiful house it is!
What a funny story he told!
What a beautiful house is it!
What a funny story did he tell!

rules.zh: 保留原句的時態 現在式： 過去式： 現在完成式： 情態動詞：
rules.en: Preserve the tense of the original sentence, whether it is present, past, present perfect or contains a modal verb.
examples: What a wonderful night it is!
What a wonderful night it was!
What a difficult week they have had!
What a difficult issue the committee must consider!

rules.zh: What 和 How 的重點不同 What 重點放在名詞 How 重點放在形容詞或副詞 兩句意思相近，但結構不同：
rules.en: What focuses on a noun phrase, whereas how focuses on an adjective or adverb. The two structures may have similar meanings, but their forms are What + noun phrase and How + adjective or adverb.
examples: What + noun phrase
How + adjective/adverb

rules.zh: 這個句型用來表達真正的感受 不要用 What 感嘆句表達完全中立、沒有感情色彩的資料。 中立資料： 強烈反應：
rules.en: Use this structure to express a genuine strong feeling, not completely neutral information with no emotional colouring.
examples: The room is ten metres long.
What a long room this is!

benefits.zh: 立即表達強烈感受 這個句型可以讓聽者立即知道你對某個人、事物或情況感到驚訝、欣賞、喜悅、失望或不滿。 比起只說一項客觀事實，感情會更加清楚。
benefits.en: It expresses a strong feeling immediately, showing surprise, admiration, joy, disappointment or dissatisfaction about a person, thing or situation more clearly than a merely objective statement.
examples: What a wonderful surprise this is!
What terrible weather we are having!

benefits.zh: 把最值得注意的事物放在前面 使用 What + noun，可以先提出你最想強調的人或事物。 一般句： 感嘆句： 第二句一開始便把 a beautiful view 放在讀者面前，重點更加突出。
benefits.en: It places the most notable thing first. What + noun foregrounds the person or thing you most want to emphasize; in the comparison, a beautiful view appears immediately and receives greater prominence.
examples: This is a beautiful view.
What a beautiful view this is!

benefits.zh: 令說話和故事更加生動 這個句型很常用於日常對話、描述經歷、講故事及回應別人的消息。 它能讓說話聽起來更有感情，而不是只像列出資料。
benefits.en: It makes speech and stories more vivid. The structure is common in everyday conversation, accounts of experiences, storytelling and reactions to news, and gives speech more feeling than a bare list of facts.
examples: What a day I have had!
What an exciting match that was!
What a lucky escape he had!

benefits.zh: 避免重複使用同一種句子開頭 學生經常重複使用： 使用 What 感嘆句，可以改變句子的組織方式： 這能令說話和寫作的句式更加多樣。
benefits.en: It avoids repeatedly using openings such as This is very, It was very or The thing is very by reorganizing the statement as a What-exclamation and adding structural variety to speech and writing.
examples: This is very...
It was very...
The thing is very...
It was a very exciting game.
What an exciting game it was!

benefits.zh: 可以自由使用完整或簡短形式 需要清楚交代人物、時間或動作時，可以使用完整句： 在簡短回應或口語中，可以省略已知資料： 因此，這個句型既適合完整描述，也適合即時反應。
benefits.en: It allows either a full or shortened form. Use a complete sentence when the person, time or action must be stated clearly, but omit information already understood in a brief spoken reaction; the pattern therefore suits both full descriptions and immediate responses.
examples: What an interesting book you chose!
What an interesting book!
